title: Radiographic manifestations of pneumatosis intestinalis and construction of an AI-assisted diagnostic system

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Radiographic manifestations of pneumatosis intestinalis and construction of an AI-assisted diagnostic system》：研究问题的原文依据。

【INTRODUCTION · s1-p1】Pneumatosis intestinalis (PI) refers to an imaging phenomenon in which gas accumulates abnormally in the submucosal or serosal layer of the intestinal wall. Its etiology spectrum spans a wide range, from benign lesions that do not require intervention (such as hormone use, endoscopic procedures, and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease) to critical lesions that require emergency surgery (such as mesenteric ischemia and intestinal necrosis), all of which can cause the same imaging manifestations.1,2 The biggest diagnostic challenge of PI lies in the highly similar imaging of benign and ischemic causes, while their treatment strategies are opposite. Delayed diagnosis can lead to extremely high mortality rates.3,4 The existing diagnostic system highly relies on the subjective experience of radiologists and lacks objective quantitative imaging grading standards, which poses a particularly prominent risk of missed diagnosis in emergency high-load scenarios. In addition, existing research lacks systematic integration of PI multimodal imaging performance, and artificial intelligence-assisted diagnosis is almost nonexistent in this field. Therefore, it is of great practical significance to systematically summarize the radiological imaging manifestations of PI and construct an AI-assisted auxiliary diagnostic system for improving diagnostic accuracy and guiding rapid clinical decision-making.

【INTRODUCTION · s1-p2】In terms of radiological imaging studies, existing research has accumulated a certain amount of information on the imaging features of PI, but the systematic and quantitative level is insufficient. In terms of x-ray plain films, Lassandro et al. analyzed the abdominal x-ray plain films of patients, which can detect intestinal wall gas accumulation, but the overall sensitivity of plain films is low, and a large number of early cases are missed.5 In terms of CT imaging, Graber et al. investigated the predictive factors for short-term mortality in patients with suspected mesenteric ischemia who underwent abdominal CT examination and showed PI, but this study did not include a systematic evaluation of accompanying signs.6 Fleck et al. included a total of 226 patients with intestinal wall enhancement (PI) detected by abdominal CT examination, and retrospectively extracted various variables during CT examination from the medical records. However, its research sample only comes from a single center, and its generalization is questionable.7 In summary, there are three core shortcomings in existing imaging research: the lack of systematic integration of multimodal imaging manifestations, the absence of accompanying signs in a unified evaluation framework, and the lack of an objective quantitative grading system validated by multiple centers.8

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Radiographic manifestations of pneumatosis intestinalis and construction of an AI-assisted diagnostic system》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Data collection and patient admission and exclusion standards · s4A-p1】This study is a multicenter retrospective study that collected consecutive cases of PI diagnosed clinically or pathologically from one tertiary hospital in North China, East China, and South China (referred to as Center A, Center B, and Center C, respectively) between January 2022 and June 2025. Due to the retrospective nature of the study and the de-identification of all data prior to analysis, patient informed consent was exempted.

【Data collection and patient admission and exclusion standards · s4A-p2】Patients must meet the following conditions to be included in this study: PI confirmed by clinical findings (typical imaging findings+follow-up outcomes) or surgical pathology; complete abdominal x-ray plain film data (upright and supine positions) and abdominal enhanced CT data (including plain scan, arterial phase, portal phase); qualified CT image quality, with no significant motion or metal artifacts that affect the interpretation. Table I summarizes scanner/protocol differences and potential distribution shifts between development and external cohorts.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Radiographic manifestations of pneumatosis intestinalis and construction of an AI-assisted diagnostic system》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Results of the Level 1 X-ray screening model · s5D-p1】To visually demonstrate the core performance indicators of the Level 1 plain x-ray rapid screening model (EfficientNet-B3) on the internal test set, including sensitivity, specificity, and inference speed, and to verify the feasibility and accuracy of this model in rapidly triaging PI in emergency scenarios, Fig. 5 clearly compares and assesses the model's balance between reducing the missed diagnosis rate (high sensitivity) and reducing unnecessary CT examinations (high specificity), while also clarifying whether its second-level inference speed meets real-time clinical needs.

【Results of the Level 1 X-ray screening model · s5D-p2】In Fig. 5, the sensitivity is 92.1% (95% CI: 87.6%–96.6%), the specificity is 84.6% (95% CI: 77.8%–91.4%), and the inference speed is 0.8 s per sheet. The error line represents the 95% confidence interval. The results showed that the model achieved over 92% sensitivity while maintaining high specificity, and the inference time for a single image was under 1 s, meeting the requirements for rapid emergency screening.
